sanskrit: devatābhyo namaskṛtya gurubhyaś caiva sarvaśaḥ utsasarja śivaṃ dhyāyann astram astreṇa śāmyatām
english: Having made obeisance to the gods and to all his teachers, and meditating upon what was auspicious, he loosed the weapon, that it might be quelled by the other weapon.

sanskrit: tatas tad astraṃ sahasā sṛṣṭaṃ gāṇḍīvadhanvanā prajajvāla mahārciṣmad yugāntānalasaṃnibham
english: Then that weapon, suddenly let loose by the wielder of Gāṇḍīva, blazed up with a vast flaming radiance, like the fire that consumes the world at the end of an age.

sanskrit: tathaiva droṇaputrasya tad astraṃ tigmatejasaḥ prajajvāla mahājvālaṃ tejomaṇḍalasaṃvṛtam
english: In like manner the weapon of Droṇa's son, fierce in its splendour, blazed forth with mighty flames, wrapped about by an orb of dazzling fire.

sanskrit: nirghātā bahavaś cāsan petur ulkāḥ sahasraśaḥ mahad bhayaṃ ca bhūtānāṃ sarveṣāṃ samajāyata
english: Many thunderclaps were heard, and meteors fell by the thousands; and a great terror arose among all living beings.

sanskrit: saśabdam abhavad vyoma jvālāmālākulaṃ bhṛśam cacāla ca mahī kṛtsnā saparvatavanadrumā
english: The sky grew loud with sound and was thickly aswarm with garlands of flame; and the whole earth trembled, with its mountains, forests, and trees.

sanskrit: te astre tejasā lokāṃs tāpayantī vyavasthite maharṣī sahitau tatra darśayām āsatus tadā
english: As those two weapons stood poised, scorching the worlds with their fiery power, two great seers thereupon showed themselves together in that place.

sanskrit: nāradaḥ sa ca dharmātmā bharatānāṃ pitāmahaḥ ubhau śamayituṃ vīrau bhāradvājadhanaṃjayau
english: They were Nārada and the righteous-souled grandsire of the Bharatas, come to pacify both those heroes, the son of Bharadvāja and Dhanaṃjaya.

sanskrit: tau munī sarvadharmajñau sarvabhūtahitaiṣiṇau dīptayor astrayor madhye sthitau paramatejasau
english: Those two sages, knowers of all the laws of righteousness, devoted to the welfare of all beings and of surpassing splendour, took their stand between the two blazing weapons.

sanskrit: tadantaram anādhṛṣyāv upagamya yaśasvinau āstām ṛṣivarau tatra jvalitāv iva pāvakau
english: Drawing near into that space between, the two illustrious and irresistible seers stood there, like two flaming fires.

sanskrit: prāṇabhṛdbhir anādhṛṣyau devadānavasaṃmatau astratejaḥ śamayituṃ lokānāṃ hitakāmyayā
english: Unassailable by any breathing creature and honoured by gods and dānavas alike, they came to quell the fire of those weapons, out of their desire for the good of the worlds.

sanskrit: ṛṣī ūcatuḥ nānāśastravidaḥ pūrve ye 'py atītā mahārathāḥ naitad astraṃ manuṣyeṣu taiḥ prayuktaṃ kathaṃ cana
english: The two seers said: Even those great chariot-warriors of old, now departed, who were versed in weapons of every kind — never did any of them employ this weapon against men.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca dṛṣṭvaiva naraśārdūlas tāv agnisamatejasau saṃjahāra śaraṃ divyaṃ tvaramāṇo dhanaṃjayaḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: The very moment that tiger among men, Dhanaṃjaya, beheld those two whose splendour matched fire, he made haste and withdrew his celestial arrow.

sanskrit: uvāca vadatāṃ śreṣṭhas tāv ṛṣī prāñjalis tadā prayuktam astram astreṇa śāmyatām iti vai mayā
english: Then that foremost of speakers said to the two seers, with joined palms: It was by me that this weapon was loosed, only that it might be quelled by the other weapon.

sanskrit: saṃhṛte paramāstre 'smin sarvān asmān aśeṣataḥ pāpakarmā dhruvaṃ drauṇiḥ pradhakṣyaty astratejasā
english: If I withdraw this supreme weapon, the evil-doer Droṇa's son will surely burn us all, every one, with the fire of his weapon.

sanskrit: atra yad dhitam asmākaṃ lokānāṃ caiva sarvathā bhavantau devasaṃkāśau tathā saṃhartum arhataḥ
english: In this matter, you two who are like the gods should by all means bring about whatever is for the good both of us and of the worlds.

sanskrit: ity uktvā saṃjahārāstraṃ punar eva dhanaṃjayaḥ saṃhāro duṣkaras tasya devair api hi saṃyuge
english: Having spoken thus, Dhanaṃjaya again withdrew his weapon — though the withdrawing of it in battle is hard even for the gods.

sanskrit: visṛṣṭasya raṇe tasya paramāstrasya saṃgrahe na śaktaḥ pāṇḍavād anyaḥ sākṣād api śatakratuḥ
english: To recall that supreme weapon once let loose in battle, none save the son of Pāṇḍu is able — not even the performer of a hundred sacrifices himself.

sanskrit: brahmatejobhavaṃ tad dhi visṛṣṭam akṛtātmanā na śakyam āvartayituṃ brahmacārivratād ṛte
english: For that weapon, born of the power of Brahman and loosed by one of unperfected soul, cannot be turned back by any save him who keeps the vow of chastity.

sanskrit: acīrṇabrahmacaryo yaḥ sṛṣṭvāvartayate punaḥ tad astraṃ sānubandhasya mūrdhānaṃ tasya kṛntati
english: Whoever, not having kept the vow of chastity, looses it and then would turn it back — that weapon severs his head, together with all his kin.

sanskrit: brahmacārī vratī cāpi duravāpam avāpya tat paramavyasanārto 'pi nārjuno 'straṃ vyamuñcata
english: But Arjuna, being chaste and faithful to his vow, had gained that hard-won weapon; and even afflicted by the gravest peril, he did not let it fly.

sanskrit: satyavratadharaḥ śūro brahmacārī ca pāṇḍavaḥ guruvartī ca tenāstraṃ saṃjahārārjunaḥ punaḥ
english: Holding to the vow of truth, a hero, chaste, and obedient to his teacher — for these reasons the son of Pāṇḍu, Arjuna, again withdrew the weapon.

sanskrit: drauṇir apy atha saṃprekṣya tāv ṛṣī purataḥ sthitau na śaśāka punar ghoram astraṃ saṃhartum āhave
english: But Droṇa's son, beholding the two seers standing before him, was not able to withdraw again his dreadful weapon in the battle.

sanskrit: aśaktaḥ pratisaṃhāre paramāstrasya saṃyuge drauṇir dīnamanā rājan dvaipāyanam abhāṣata
english: Unable to recall that supreme weapon in the fray, Droṇa's son, with downcast heart, O king, spoke thus to Dvaipāyana:

sanskrit: uttamavyasanārtena prāṇatrāṇam abhīpsunā mayaitad astram utsṛṣṭaṃ bhīmasenabhayān mune
english: Afflicted by the direst peril and longing to save my life, it was by me, O sage, that this weapon was loosed, out of fear of Bhīmasena.

sanskrit: adharmaś ca kṛto 'nena dhārtarāṣṭraṃ jighāṃsatā mithyācāreṇa bhagavan bhīmasenena saṃyuge
english: And a deed against righteousness was done by Bhīmasena, O blessed one, when through treacherous conduct in battle he sought to slay the son of Dhṛtarāṣṭra.

sanskrit: ataḥ sṛṣṭam idaṃ brahman mayāstram akṛtātmanā tasya bhūyo 'dya saṃhāraṃ kartuṃ nāham ihotsahe
english: Therefore was this weapon loosed by me, O brāhmaṇa, by one of unperfected soul; and now I have no power here to bring about its withdrawal again.

sanskrit: visṛṣṭaṃ hi mayā divyam etad astraṃ durāsadam apāṇḍavāyeti mune vahnitejo 'numantrya vai
english: For this celestial and irresistible weapon was loosed by me, O sage, with the spell pronounced upon its fiery power, that there be no son of Pāṇḍu left.

sanskrit: tad idaṃ pāṇḍaveyānām antakāyābhisaṃhitam adya pāṇḍusutān sarvāñ jīvitād bhraṃśayiṣyati
english: This weapon, then, aimed at the destruction of the descendants of Pāṇḍu, will this very day strip all the sons of Pāṇḍu of their lives.

sanskrit: kṛtaṃ pāpam idaṃ brahman roṣāviṣṭena cetasā vadham āśāsya pārthānāṃ mayāstraṃ sṛjatā raṇe
english: This evil deed was done by me, O brāhmaṇa, with a mind possessed by rage, when, longing for the death of the sons of Pṛthā, I loosed the weapon in battle.

sanskrit: vyāsa uvāca astraṃ brahmaśiras tāta vidvān pārtho dhanaṃjayaḥ utsṛṣṭavān na roṣeṇa na vadhāya tavāhave
english: Vyāsa said: The son of Pṛthā, Dhanaṃjaya, in his knowledge, my son, loosed the weapon Brahmaśiras neither out of wrath nor to slay you in the battle.

sanskrit: astram astreṇa tu raṇe tava saṃśamayiṣyatā visṛṣṭam arjunenedaṃ punaś ca pratisaṃhṛtam
english: It was loosed by Arjuna only that your weapon might be quelled in battle by another weapon; and again he has withdrawn it.

sanskrit: brahmāstram apy avāpyaitad upadeśāt pitus tava kṣatradharmān mahābāhur nākampata dhanaṃjayaḥ
english: Though he had gained this very weapon of Brahman through the teaching of your father, the mighty-armed Dhanaṃjaya did not waver from the duty of a kṣatriya.

sanskrit: evaṃ dhṛtimataḥ sādhoḥ sarvāstraviduṣaḥ sataḥ sabhrātṛbandhoḥ kasmāt tvaṃ vadham asya cikīrṣasi
english: Why, then, do you seek the death of one so steadfast, so virtuous, so versed in all weapons, together with his brothers and kinsmen?

sanskrit: astraṃ brahmaśiro yatra paramāstreṇa vadhyate samā dvādaśa parjanyas tad rāṣṭraṃ nābhivarṣati
english: In whatever realm the weapon Brahmaśiras is met and overcome by another supreme weapon, for twelve years the rain-cloud sends no rain upon that land.

sanskrit: etadarthaṃ mahābāhuḥ śaktimān api pāṇḍavaḥ na vihanty etad astraṃ te prajāhitacikīrṣayā
english: For this reason the mighty-armed son of Pāṇḍu, though he has the power, does not strike down this weapon of yours — out of his wish for the welfare of the people.

sanskrit: pāṇḍavās tvaṃ ca rāṣṭraṃ ca sadā saṃrakṣyam eva naḥ tasmāt saṃhara divyaṃ tvam astram etan mahābhuja
english: The Pāṇḍavas, and you, and the realm are ever to be protected by us; therefore, O mighty-armed one, withdraw this celestial weapon of yours.

sanskrit: aroṣas tava caivāstu pārthāḥ santu nirāmayāḥ na hy adharmeṇa rājarṣiḥ pāṇḍavo jetum icchati
english: Let your wrath be stilled, and let the sons of Pṛthā be unharmed; for the royal seer, the son of Pāṇḍu, does not wish to conquer by unrighteous means.

sanskrit: maṇiṃ caitaṃ prayacchaibhyo yas te śirasi tiṣṭhati etad ādāya te prāṇān pratidāsyanti pāṇḍavāḥ
english: And give over to them this jewel that rests upon your head; taking it, the Pāṇḍavas will grant you back your life.

sanskrit: drauṇir uvāca pāṇḍavair yāni ratnāni yac cānyat kauravair dhanam avāptānīha tebhyo 'yaṃ maṇir mama viśiṣyate
english: Droṇa's son said: Of all the gems won here by the Pāṇḍavas and whatever other wealth was won by the Kauravas, this jewel of mine is the surpassing one.

sanskrit: yam ābadhya bhayaṃ nāsti śastravyādhikṣudhāśrayam devebhyo dānavebhyo vā nāgebhyo vā kathaṃ cana
english: Bearing it bound upon oneself, there is no fear arising from weapon, disease, or hunger, none whatever from gods, dānavas, or nāgas.

sanskrit: na ca rakṣogaṇabhayaṃ na taskarabhayaṃ tathā evaṃvīryo maṇir ayaṃ na me tyājyaḥ kathaṃ cana
english: Nor is there fear of the hosts of rākṣasas, nor any fear of thieves. Of such potency is this jewel; it is by no means to be given up by me.

sanskrit: yat tu me bhagavān āha tan me kāryam anantaram ayaṃ maṇir ayaṃ cāham iṣīkā nipatiṣyati garbheṣu pāṇḍaveyānām amoghaṃ caitad udyatam
english: But what the blessed one bids me — that must I forthwith do. Here is the jewel, and here am I; yet this blade of reed shall fall upon the unborn of the Pāṇḍavas, for once raised it does not fail.

sanskrit: vyāsa uvāca evaṃ kuru na cānyā te buddhiḥ kāryā kadā cana garbheṣu pāṇḍaveyānāṃ visṛjyaitad upārama
english: Vyāsa said: Do thus, and let no other purpose ever be formed by you. Loose it upon the unborn of the Pāṇḍavas, and then desist.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tataḥ paramam astraṃ tad aśvatthāmā bhṛśāturaḥ dvaipāyanavacaḥ śrutvā garbheṣu pramumoca ha
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Then Aśvatthāman, sorely afflicted, having heard the word of Dvaipāyana, loosed that supreme weapon upon the unborn children.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tad ājñāya hṛṣīkeśo visṛṣṭaṃ pāpakarmaṇā hṛṣyamāṇa idaṃ vākyaṃ drauṇiṃ pratyabravīt tadā
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Perceiving that the weapon had been loosed by the doer of evil, Hṛṣīkeśa, well-pleased, then spoke this word in answer to Droṇa's son:

sanskrit: virāṭasya sutāṃ pūrvaṃ snuṣāṃ gāṇḍīvadhanvanaḥ upaplavyagatāṃ dṛṣṭvā vratavān brāhmaṇo 'bravīt
english: Long ago, beholding the daughter of Virāṭa, the daughter-in-law of the wielder of Gāṇḍīva, as she dwelt at Upaplavya, a brāhmaṇa faithful to his vows declared:

sanskrit: parikṣīṇeṣu kuruṣu putras tava janiṣyati etad asya parikṣittvaṃ garbhasthasya bhaviṣyati
english: When the Kurus are wasted away, a son shall be born to you; and this — being thus born in a perished line — shall be his title of Parīkṣit, even while he lies in the womb.

sanskrit: tasya tad vacanaṃ sādhoḥ satyam eva bhaviṣyati parikṣid bhavitā hy eṣāṃ punar vaṃśakaraḥ sutaḥ
english: That word of the virtuous one shall surely come to pass: Parīkṣit indeed shall be theirs, a son who once more shall carry on the line.

sanskrit: evaṃ bruvāṇaṃ govindaṃ sātvatapravaraṃ tadā drauṇiḥ paramasaṃrabdhaḥ pratyuvācedam uttaram
english: To Govinda, foremost of the Sātvatas, as he spoke thus, Droṇa's son, in utmost fury, then made this reply:

sanskrit: naitad evaṃ yathāttha tvaṃ pakṣapātena keśava vacanaṃ puṇḍarīkākṣa na ca madvākyam anyathā
english: It is not as you say, out of partiality, O Keśava; not so is your word, O lotus-eyed one, nor shall my own word prove otherwise.

sanskrit: patiṣyaty etad astraṃ hi garbhe tasyā mayodyatam virāṭaduhituḥ kṛṣṇa yāṃ tvaṃ rakṣitum icchasi
english: For this weapon, raised by me, shall fall upon the embryo of that daughter of Virāṭa, O Kṛṣṇa, whom you wish to protect.

sanskrit: vāsudeva uvāca amoghaḥ paramāstrasya pātas tasya bhaviṣyati sa tu garbho mṛto jāto dīrgham āyur avāpsyati
english: Vāsudeva said: The fall of that supreme weapon shall indeed not fail; yet that embryo, though born dead, shall attain a long life.

sanskrit: tvāṃ tu kāpuruṣaṃ pāpaṃ viduḥ sarve manīṣiṇaḥ asakṛt pāpakarmāṇaṃ bālajīvitaghātakam
english: But you all the wise know to be a coward and a sinner, again and again a worker of evil, a slayer of the lives of children.

sanskrit: tasmāt tvam asya pāpasya karmaṇaḥ phalam āpnuhi trīṇi varṣasahasrāṇi cariṣyasi mahīm imām aprāpnuvan kva cit kāṃ cit saṃvidaṃ jātu kena cit
english: Therefore receive the fruit of this evil deed: for three thousand years you shall wander over this earth, nowhere ever finding fellowship of speech with anyone.

sanskrit: nirjanān asahāyas tvaṃ deśān pravicariṣyasi bhavitrī na hi te kṣudra janamadhyeṣu saṃsthitiḥ
english: Companionless, you shall roam through desolate lands; for there shall be no abiding for you, base one, in the midst of men.

sanskrit: pūyaśoṇitagandhī ca durgakāntārasaṃśrayaḥ vicariṣyasi pāpātman sarvavyādhisamanvitaḥ
english: Reeking of pus and blood, taking refuge in trackless wastes and wilderness, you shall wander, O evil-souled one, beset by every disease.

sanskrit: vayaḥ prāpya parikṣit tu vedavratam avāpya ca kṛpāc chāradvatād vīraḥ sarvāstrāṇy upalapsyate
english: But Parīkṣit, attaining to manhood and gaining the vows of the Veda, that hero, shall obtain all weapons from Kṛpa, the son of Śaradvat.

sanskrit: viditvā paramāstrāṇi kṣatradharmavrate sthitaḥ ṣaṣṭiṃ varṣāṇi dharmātmā vasudhāṃ pālayiṣyati
english: Having mastered the supreme weapons and standing firm in the vow of a kṣatriya's duty, the righteous-souled one shall guard the earth for sixty years.

sanskrit: itaś cordhvaṃ mahābāhuḥ kururājo bhaviṣyati parikṣin nāma nṛpatir miṣatas te sudurmate paśya me tapaso vīryaṃ satyasya ca narādhama
english: And from this time onward there shall be a mighty-armed king of the Kurus, a sovereign named Parīkṣit, before your very eyes, O most wicked one. Behold, O basest of men, the power of my austerity and of my truth.

sanskrit: vyāsa uvāca yasmād anādṛtya kṛtaṃ tvayāsmān karma dāruṇam brāhmaṇasya sataś caiva yasmāt te vṛttam īdṛśam
english: Vyāsa said: Inasmuch as, disregarding us, you have wrought this dreadful deed, and inasmuch as such has been your conduct, even though you are a brāhmaṇa —

sanskrit: tasmād yad devakīputra uktavān uttamaṃ vacaḥ asaṃśayaṃ te tad bhāvi kṣudrakarman vrajāśv itaḥ
english: therefore that noble word which the son of Devakī has spoken shall without doubt come to pass for you, O doer of base deeds. Go hence at once.

sanskrit: aśvatthāmovāca sahaiva bhavatā brahman sthāsyāmi puruṣeṣv aham satyavāg astu bhagavān ayaṃ ca puruṣottamaḥ
english: Aśvatthāman said: Together with you, O brāhmaṇa, shall I dwell among men. Let this blessed one, this best of men, be one whose word is truth.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca pradāyātha maṇiṃ drauṇiḥ pāṇḍavānāṃ mahātmanām jagāma vimanās teṣāṃ sarveṣāṃ paśyatāṃ vanam
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Then, having given over the jewel to the great-souled Pāṇḍavas, Droṇa's son, dejected in mind, departed into the forest while they all looked on.

sanskrit: pāṇḍavāś cāpi govindaṃ puraskṛtya hatadviṣaḥ kṛṣṇadvaipāyanaṃ caiva nāradaṃ ca mahāmunim
english: And the Pāṇḍavas, their foes now slain, setting Govinda before them, and Kṛṣṇa Dvaipāyana, and the great sage Nārada —

sanskrit: droṇaputrasya sahajaṃ maṇim ādāya satvarāḥ draupadīm abhyadhāvanta prāyopetāṃ manasvinīm
english: taking up the jewel born with the son of Droṇa, they hastened in all speed toward the high-minded Draupadī, who had resolved to fast unto death.

sanskrit: tatas te puruṣavyāghrāḥ sadaśvair anilopamaiḥ abhyayuḥ sahadāśārhāḥ śibiraṃ punar eva ha
english: Then those tigers among men, together with the one of the Dāśārha line, came once again to the encampment, borne by their fine steeds swift as the wind.

sanskrit: avatīrya rathābhyāṃ tu tvaramāṇā mahārathāḥ dadṛśur draupadīṃ kṛṣṇām ārtām ārtatarāḥ svayam
english: Descending in haste from their two chariots, those great chariot-warriors, themselves more stricken still, beheld Draupadī, the dark one, in her grief.

sanskrit: tām upetya nirānandāṃ duḥkhaśokasamanvitām parivārya vyatiṣṭhanta pāṇḍavāḥ sahakeśavāḥ
english: Drawing near to her, joyless and overwhelmed with sorrow and grief, the Pāṇḍavas, together with Keśava, stood gathered about her.

sanskrit: tato rājñābhyanujñāto bhīmaseno mahābalaḥ pradadau tu maṇiṃ divyaṃ vacanaṃ cedam abravīt
english: Then Bhīmasena of mighty strength, having been bidden by the king, presented the celestial jewel and spoke this word:

sanskrit: ayaṃ bhadre tava maṇiḥ putrahantā jitaḥ sa te uttiṣṭha śokam utsṛjya kṣatradharmam anusmara
english: Here, gentle lady, is your jewel; the slayer of your sons has been overcome for you. Rise up, cast off your grief, and call to mind the duty of a kṣatriya.

sanskrit: prayāṇe vāsudevasya śamārtham asitekṣaṇe yāny uktāni tvayā bhīru vākyāni madhughātinaḥ
english: When Vāsudeva set out to make peace, O dark-eyed lady, those words you spoke, O timid one, to the slayer of Madhu —

sanskrit: naiva me patayaḥ santi na putrā bhrātaro na ca naiva tvam api govinda śamam icchati rājani
english: "I have no husbands left, nor sons, nor brothers; and not even you, O Govinda, desires peace with the king" —

sanskrit: uktavaty asi dhīrāṇi vākyāni puruṣottamam kṣatradharmānurūpāṇi tāni saṃsmartum arhasi
english: resolute words you spoke then to that best of men, words befitting the duty of a kṣatriya — those you ought now to call to mind.

sanskrit: hato duryodhanaḥ pāpo rājyasya paripanthakaḥ duḥśāsanasya rudhiraṃ pītaṃ visphurato mayā
english: The wicked Duryodhana, who barred the way to the kingdom, is slain; and the blood of Duḥśāsana, as he quivered, was drunk by me.

sanskrit: vairasya gatam ānṛṇyaṃ na sma vācyā vivakṣatām jitvā mukto droṇaputro brāhmaṇyād gauraveṇa ca
english: The debt of our enmity is discharged; we shall not be reproached by those who would find fault. The son of Droṇa, though conquered, was set free, out of regard for his brahmanhood and his honour.

sanskrit: yaśo 'sya pātitaṃ devi śarīraṃ tv avaśeṣitam viyojitaś ca maṇinā nyāsitaś cāyudhaṃ bhuvi
english: His glory has been cast down, O lady, though his body alone is left; he has been parted from his jewel and made to lay down his weapon upon the ground.

sanskrit: draupady uvāca kevalānṛṇyam āptāsmi guruputro gurur mama śirasy etaṃ maṇiṃ rājā pratibadhnātu bhārata
english: Draupadī said: I have attained release from my whole debt. The teacher's son is as a teacher to me. Let the king bind this jewel upon his head, O descendant of Bharata.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca taṃ gṛhītvā tato rājā śirasy evākarot tadā guror ucchiṣṭam ity eva draupadyā vacanād api
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Then the king took it and set it upon his own head, holding it, at Draupadī's word, as a thing left by a teacher.

sanskrit: tato divyaṃ maṇivaraṃ śirasā dhārayan prabhuḥ śuśubhe sa mahārājaḥ sacandra iva parvataḥ
english: Then the lord, bearing upon his head that excellent celestial jewel, that great king shone resplendent, like a mountain crowned with the moon.

sanskrit: uttasthau putraśokārtā tataḥ kṛṣṇā manasvinī kṛṣṇaṃ cāpi mahābāhuṃ paryapṛcchata dharmarāṭ
english: Then the high-minded Kṛṣṇā, stricken with grief for her sons, rose up; and the King of Righteousness questioned the mighty-armed Kṛṣṇa.
